learning_outcomes.text: Correctly name and formulate inorganic compounds according to international standards.
Recognize the main functional groups of organic compounds.
Link chemical elements to their symbols and deduce their properties according to their position in the periodic table.
Determine the quantitative relationships between the elements of a compound and between substances when they undergo a chemical change.
Describe the structure of the atom, and relate the electronic configurations of chemical elements to their properties and reactivity.
Identify the chemical bonding present in molecules and describe the theoretical models on which they are based.
Determine the geometry and polar character of simple molecules.
Describe the states of aggregation and interpret their physical properties based on the type of intermolecular forces present.
Identify the main chemical equilibria in aqueous solutions.
Illustrate the main aspects of the reactivity of inorganic and organic compounds and their applications to Engineering.

syllabus_topics: MATTER AND MEASUREMENT. Classification of matter: elements, compounds, molecular compounds, ionic compounds, organic compounds, inorganic compounds, mixtures and separation of mixtures. Measurements: units, precision, accuracy, significant figures, and dimensional analysis. Properties of substances.
THE ATOM AND ITS COMPONENTS. Atoms and atomic theory. Components of the atom. Atomic number and mass number. Isotopes. Nuclear stability and radioactivity.

MASS RELATIONSHIPS IN CHEMISTRY: STOICHIOMETRY. Atomic masses. Mol. Molar mass. Stoichiometric laws. Stoichiometric calculations of compounds. Chemical reactions and equations. Balancing chemical equations. Types of reactions. Quantitative information from chemical equations. Limiting reactant. Reaction yield. Simultaneous and consecutive reactions. Concentration of solutions: molarity.

CHEMICAL NOMENCLATURE AND FORMULATION. Formulation and nomenclature of inorganic substances: elements, cations, anions, oxides, peroxides, binary hydrogen compounds, metal-nonmetal compounds, nonmetal-nonmetal compounds, heteropolyatomic cations, hydroxides, oxoacids, oxoacid ions, oxosalts, acidic oxosalts, and hydrates. Nomenclature and formulation of organic compounds: alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and some functional groups containing oxygen and nitrogen.
REACTIONS IN AQUEOUS SOLUTION. Aqueous solutions. Precipitation reactions. Acid-base reactions. Oxidation-reduction reactions. Balancing redox reactions.

ELECTRONIC STRUCTURE AND THE PERIODIC TABLE. Light and atomic spectra. The hydrogen spectrum. Bohr model. Wave nature of the electron. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle. Quantum mechanical model. Quantum numbers. Atomic orbitals. Multi-electron atoms. Electronic configurations. Periodic trends of atomic properties.
CHEMICAL BONDS. Lewis theory. Types of chemical bonds. Lewis structures. Polar molecules. Formal charges. Resonance. Exceptions to the octet rule. Bond order and bond length.
MOLECULAR SHAPE AND STRUCTURE. Molecular geometry: VSEPR model. Molecular orbital theory. Valence bond theory. Hybridization of atomic orbitals. Multiple covalent bonding. The bonding in metals.

GASES. Properties of gases. Characterization of a gas. The ideal gas law and applications. Gas mixtures: humid gases, partial pressure, and mole fraction. Kinetic-molecular theory of gases, gas properties, and internal energy. Molecular velocity distribution. Diffusion and effusion of gases. Graham's law. Real gases. Van der Waals equation.
LIQUIDS AND SOLIDS. Kinetic-molecular description of liquids and solids. Intermolecular attractions. Properties of liquids. Solid state. Phase changes. Phase equilibria. Phase diagrams.
MIXTURES. Concentration of solutions. Fundamentals of solubility. Colligative properties of solutions. Colloidal mixtures.
CHEMICAL EQUILIBRIUM. Basic concepts of chemical equilibrium. Equilibrium constant. Factors that affect equilibrium. Le Châtelier's principle.
REDOX REACTIONS. Voltaic cells. Electrode potentials. Nernst equation. Batteries and cells. Electrolytic cells. Electrolysis of water.
ACID-BASE REACTIONS. Water autoionization. pH scale. Strength of acids and bases. Ka and Kb. Hydrolysis.
PRECIPITATION REACTIONS. Solubility. Solubility product constant. Effect of temperature and pressure on solubility. Dissolution of precipitates.
PRACTICE 1: Determination of liquid densities.
PRACTICE 2: Preparation of solutions.
PRACTICE 3: Studies of different types of equilibria in solution.
PRACTICE 4: Recognition of organic functions.
PRACTICE 5: Oxidation-reduction reactions.
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes (lectures) using audiovisual aids to explain basic aspects, fostering discussion and critical thinking.
Problem-solving classes where typical problems are solved by the professor and similar problems are assigned for student practice.
Introductory laboratory seminars explaining theoretical foundations and experimental procedures.
Laboratory practices, consisting of five experimental sessions designed to complement student training.
Academic-formative tutorials in small groups, focusing on problem-solving and clarification of theoretical concepts.
General tutorials for resolving doubts, available in person and through the virtual classroom.
Group work (project) on the importance of Chemistry in industrial, economic, environmental, and social contexts, including a video presentation in English.
Use of the virtual classroom as a support tool for documentation, task management, and online quizzes.

assessment_methods.method: Quizzes and exercises in academic tutorials
Course project (group work, video presentation in English)
Attitude, skill, and work method in the laboratory
Four reasoned interventions in English in the course project forum
Final exam (written test of problems and questions)

assessment_rules: The continuous assessment mode requires students to achieve a minimum score of 3.5 out of 10 for objective tests, a minimum of 5.0 out of 10 for laboratory practices, and a minimum of 4.0 out of 10 for the final exam. To pass the course, an overall grade of at least 5.0 out of 10 is required. If the minimum requirements for objective tests, laboratory practices, or the final exam are not met, the final grade cannot exceed 4.5. Individual theme activities and tutorial exercises are recoverable, and laboratory practices or a laboratory exam can be retaken if minimum scores or attendance are not met.
